SpaceCenter.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Provides functionality to interact with Kerbal Space Program. This includes controlling
the active vessel, managing its resources, planning maneuver nodes and auto-piloting.
</summary>
</doc>

LaunchVessel.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Launch a vessel.
</summary>
<param name="craftDirectory">Name of the directory in the current saves
"Ships" directory, that contains the craft file.
For example <c>"VAB"</c> or <c>"SPH"</c>.</param>
<param name="name">Name of the vessel to launch. This is the name of the ".craft" file
in the save directory, without the ".craft" file extension.</param>
<param name="launchSite">Name of the launch site. For example <c>"LaunchPad"</c> or
<c>"Runway"</c>.</param>
<param name="crew">A list of names of Kerbals to place in the craft. Pass an empty list to use default crew assignments.</param>
<param name="recover">If true and there is a vessel on the launch site,
recover it before launching.</param>
<param name="flagUrl">If not <c>null</c>, the asset URL of the mission flag to use for the launch.</param>
<remarks>
Throws an exception if any of the games pre-flight checks fail.
</remarks>
</doc>

CanRailsWarpAt.documentation: Returns true if regular "on-rails" time warp can be used, at the specified warp . The maximum time warp rate is limited by various things, including how close the active vessel is to a planet. See the KSP wiki for details. The warp factor to check.

WarpTo.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Uses time acceleration to warp forward to a time in the future, specified
by universal time <paramref name="ut" />. This call blocks until the desired
time is reached. Uses regular "on-rails" or physical time warp as appropriate.
For example, physical time warp is used when the active vessel is traveling
through an atmosphere. When using regular "on-rails" time warp, the warp
rate is limited by <paramref name="maxRailsRate" />, and when using physical
time warp, the warp rate is limited by <paramref name="maxPhysicsRate" />.
</summary>
<param name="ut">The universal time to warp to, in seconds.</param>
<param name="maxRailsRate">The maximum warp rate in regular "on-rails" time warp.
</param>
<param name="maxPhysicsRate">The maximum warp rate in physical time warp.</param>
<returns>When the time warp is complete.</returns>
</doc>

AutoPilot_Reset.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Disengages the auto-pilot and resets all configuration parameters to their defaults.
Also resets the target pitch, heading and roll, and clears all internal controller

persists across engagements so that a craft known to be flexible re-latches quickly.
</summary>
</doc>

AutoPilot_TargetPitchAndHeading.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Set target pitch and heading angles.
</summary>
<param name="pitch">Target pitch angle, in degrees between -90° and +90°.</param>
<param name="heading">Target heading angle, in degrees between 0° and 360°.</param>
<remarks>
A convenience for aiming the nose by angle; heading is ill-defined when the nose is near
vertical (pitch → ±90°), so near the vertical prefer <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.TargetDirection" /> or
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.SetDirectionAndUp" />. Preserves the current roll relative to
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.UpReference" />.
</remarks>
</doc>

AutoPilot_SetDirectionAndUp.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Set the target attitude from a nose direction and an up vector: point the nose along
<paramref name="direction" /> and roll so the vessel's dorsal (roof) axis aligns with
<paramref name="up" /> (its component perpendicular to the nose), then apply an optional
<paramref name="roll" /> offset about the nose. Both vectors are in the reference frame
specified by <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.ReferenceFrame" />.
</summary>
<param name="direction">The direction to point the nose in.</param>
<param name="up">The reference direction the roof is rolled towards. Need not be
normalized or perpendicular to <paramref name="direction" /> — its component perpendicular
to the nose is used. Stored as the <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.UpReference" />.</param>
<param name="roll">An additional roll about the nose, in degrees (positive banks right).
Defaults to 0.</param>
<remarks>
This is the way to hold a well-defined orientation through a maneuver — for example a
gravity turn: pass a fixed <paramref name="up" /> (say north) and the roll stays defined the
whole way, with no singularity at the vertical. It is well-defined for every nose direction
except <paramref name="up" /> parallel to <paramref name="direction" /> (asking the roof to
point where the nose already points), where it falls back to pointing the nose only.
Equivalent to setting <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.UpReference" /> to <paramref name="up" />, aiming at
<paramref name="direction" /> and setting <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.TargetRoll" /> to
<paramref name="roll" />.
</remarks>
</doc>

<summary>
Whether an in-game window showing the auto-pilot's state (engagement, attitude error,

AutoPilot_get_TargetRoll.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The target roll, in degrees, measured about the vessel's nose relative to the
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.UpReference" /> (roll 0 aligns the vessel's dorsal/roof axis with the reference;
positive roll banks right). <c>NaN</c> if no target roll is set.
</summary>
<remarks>
When left unset (<c>NaN</c>) the auto-pilot suppresses roll rotation — it drives the roll
rate to zero rather than holding a specific roll angle. Setting a value re-rolls the
current target to that angle relative to the up reference while keeping the nose direction.
With the default reference (the frame's up) this reproduces the historical roll away from
the vertical, and is ill-defined only when the nose points along the reference (near
straight up or down). To hold a well-defined roll through the vertical — for example a
gravity turn — set the up reference off the flight path (see
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.SetDirectionAndUp" /> / <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.UpReference" />).
</remarks>
</doc>

AutoPilot_get_UpReference.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>

that <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.TargetRoll" /> is measured against: at roll 0 the vessel's dorsal (roof)

effect of <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.SetDirectionAndUp" />. Setting the target rotation, target direction,
or the scalar pitch/heading leaves it unchanged. Choosing a reference off the flight path
keeps roll well-defined through the vertical.

AutoPilot_get_AttitudeError.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The per-axis attitude error (pitch, yaw, roll), in degrees, between the vessel's current
attitude and the commanded target. All three components come from one singularity-free
residual decomposition, so they stay well-defined near the vertical (unlike a subtraction
of pitch/heading/roll angles). The scalar <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.PitchError" />,
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.HeadingError" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.RollError" /> are the magnitudes of the pitch, yaw
and roll components respectively. Throws an exception if the auto-pilot has not been
engaged.
</summary>
</doc>

AutoPilot_get_PitchError.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>

Throws an exception if the auto-pilot has not been engaged.
</summary>
<remarks>
The pitch component of <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.AttitudeError" /> — the pitch part of the direction error
resolved in the roll-invariant frame, well-defined near the vertical.
</remarks>
</doc>

AutoPilot_get_HeadingError.documentation:
<doc>

Throws an exception if the auto-pilot has not been engaged.

AutoPilot_get_RollError.documentation:

</doc>

AutoPilot_get_CurrentError.documentation:

AutoPilot_get_CurrentAttitudeError.documentation:

AutoPilot_get_PitchYawRateFilterMode.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Controls the rate-feedback filtering (the wobble-suppression filter on the measured
angular velocity) for the pitch and yaw axes of a structurally flexible vessel. When
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RateFilterMode.Automatic" /> (the default) the auto-pilot detects the
oscillation at runtime, estimates its frequency and routes it to the appropriate tool
(a notch filter for a low-frequency mode near the control band, a low-pass for a
high-frequency mode). <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RateFilterMode.Off" /> disables rate filtering only —
the other oscillation mitigations are unaffected. <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RateFilterMode.Notch" />
and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RateFilterMode.LowPass" /> force the respective tool unconditionally at

AutoPilot_set_PitchYawRateFilterMode.documentation:

the other oscillation mitigations are unaffected. <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RateFilterMode.Notch" />
and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RateFilterMode.LowPass" /> force the respective tool unconditionally at
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.PitchYawOscillationFrequency" />, for a vessel known in advance to be

AutoPilot_get_OscillationBandwidthFloorM.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Controls the bandwidth-floor mitigation: the reduction of the inner control loop
bandwidth on a structurally flexible axis — the primary oscillation stabilizer. When
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.MitigationMode.Automatic" /> (the default) it engages on a latched axis
while holding (and during a detected limit cycle). <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.MitigationMode.Off" />
never reduces the bandwidth; <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.MitigationMode.Forced" /> keeps it fully
reduced at all times.
</summary>
</doc>

AutoPilot_set_OscillationBandwidthFloorM.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Controls the bandwidth-floor mitigation: the reduction of the inner control loop
bandwidth on a structurally flexible axis — the primary oscillation stabilizer. When
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.MitigationMode.Automatic" /> (the default) it engages on a latched axis
while holding (and during a detected limit cycle). <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.MitigationMode.Off" />
never reduces the bandwidth; <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.MitigationMode.Forced" /> keeps it fully
reduced at all times.
</summary>
</doc>

AutoPilot_get_OscillationBandwidthFloor.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>

AutoPilot_set_OscillationBandwidthFloor.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>

bandwidth-floor mitigation is engaged on it. Lowering it suppresses oscillation more

follows the hold gate on a latched axis. <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.MitigationMode.Off" /> never cuts
the feedforward; <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.MitigationMode.Forced" /> always cuts it fully.
</summary>
</doc>

AutoPilot_set_OscillationFeedforwardMode.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>

structurally flexible axis while holding, so it cannot re-excite a residual mode at
the reduced bandwidth. When <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.MitigationMode.Automatic" /> (the default) it
follows the hold gate on a latched axis. <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.MitigationMode.Off" /> never cuts

<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.MitigationMode.Automatic" /> (the default) it engages on a latched axis

<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.MitigationMode.Off" /> never smooths; <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.MitigationMode.Forced" />
smooths fully at all times.
</summary>
</doc>

AutoPilot_set_OscillationOutputFilterMod.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>

(and, lightly, while the oscillation detector is firing on an unlatched one).

AutoPilot_get_PitchYawControlOscillation.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>

the deviation of the delivered control about its slowly-varying trim. A settled hold sits
near zero; a sustained limit cycle drives it toward 1. Read-only.
</summary>

<doc>
<summary>

detected; values approaching 1 mean a sustained structural oscillation. Read-only.
</summary>
</doc>

AutoPilot_get_PitchYawOscillationLatched.documentation:

pitch/yaw axis group, or <c>NaN</c> until the estimator acquires. The estimator runs in

AutoPilot_get_DiagnosticLogging.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
When <c>true</c>, records one row of diagnostic data per physics tick to an
in-memory buffer (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.DiagnosticLog" />), and echoes each row to
Player.log prefixed with <c>[KRPC.AP]</c>. The data is CSV: the first row is a
header naming every column, and each subsequent row records the auto-pilot's full
control-loop state for one tick (setpoints, errors, measured rates, gains,
velocity-profile and feedforward internals, control outputs, and the oscillation
detector/gate/mitigation state). The buffer is capped at 3000 data rows (one minute
at the 50 Hz physics rate); when full, this property switches itself back to
<c>false</c> and the buffer holds the minute following the enable. Setting to
<c>true</c> clears the buffer. Defaults to <c>false</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

<doc>

control-loop state for one tick (setpoints, errors, measured rates, gains,
velocity-profile and feedforward internals, control outputs, and the oscillation
detector/gate/mitigation state). The buffer is capped at 3000 data rows (one minute

</summary>

AutoPilot_get_DiagnosticLog.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The diagnostic log collected since <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.DiagnosticLogging" /> was last set to
<c>true</c>: CSV text whose first line is the column header and each subsequent
line records one physics tick. Vector-valued channels use one column per component
(suffixed <c>.p/.r/.y</c> for pitch, roll, yaw); pitch-yaw-group/roll channel pairs
are suffixed <c>.py/.roll</c>. Returns an empty string if diagnostic logging has
not been enabled or no ticks have occurred.
</summary>
</doc>

Control_GetActionGroup.documentation: Returns true if the given action group is enabled. A number between 0 and 9 inclusive, or between 0 and 250 inclusive when the Extended Action Groups mod is installed.

Control_SetActionGroup.documentation: Sets the state of the given action group. A number between 0 and 9 inclusive, or between 0 and 250 inclusive when the Extended Action Groups mod is installed.

Control_ToggleActionGroup.documentation: Toggles the state of the given action group. A number between 0 and 9 inclusive, or between 0 and 250 inclusive when the Extended Action Groups mod is installed.

Control_GetActionGroupActions.documentation: Returns a list of all the part actions that are assigned to the given action group. Each entry identifies the part, the part module, and the action's name and identifier. Returns an empty list if no actions are assigned to the group. A number between 0 and 9 inclusive, or between 0 and 250 inclusive when the Extended Action Groups mod is installed. For stock action groups, the assignments are read from each part action directly. When the Extended Action Groups mod is installed, the assignments are queried from the mod instead, so that actions assigned to its additional groups are included.

Flight_SimulateAerodynamicForceAt.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Simulate and return the total aerodynamic forces acting on the vessel,
if it were traveling with the given velocity, at the given position and
orientation, in the atmosphere of the given celestial body.
</summary>
<param name="body">The celestial body whose atmosphere the forces are simulated in.</param>
<param name="position">The position of the vessel, in reference frame
<see cref="T:SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame" />.</param>
<param name="velocity">The velocity of the vessel, in reference frame
<see cref="T:SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame" />.</param>
<param name="rotation">The orientation of the vessel, in reference frame
<see cref="T:SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame" />, in the same form as <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.Rotation" />.
The angle of attack and sideslip follow from this orientation relative to the
velocity; the roll component sets the direction of any aerodynamic lift. Pass
the vessel's current rotation to evaluate the force at its current orientation.</param>
<returns>A vector pointing in the direction that the force acts, with its
magnitude equal to the strength of the force in Newtons, in reference frame
<see cref="T:SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame" />.</returns>
<remarks>
The position, velocity and rotation arguments, and the returned force, are all
expressed in reference frame <see cref="T:SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame" />. The result is the
force the vessel would experience if it were placed at that position and
orientation with the air flowing past it at that velocity; it is the force at
the requested orientation, not the force in the vessel's current orientation.
Atmospheric temperature and density are evaluated at the current universal time.
</remarks>
</doc>

Flight_SimulateAerodynamicWrenchAt.documentation: Simulate and return the total aerodynamic force and torque acting on the vessel, if its center of mass were traveling with the given velocity, at the given position, orientation and angular velocity, in the atmosphere of the given celestial body. The celestial body whose atmosphere the wrench is simulated in. The position of the vessel's center of mass, in reference frame . The velocity of the vessel's center of mass, in reference frame . The orientation of the vessel, in reference frame , in the same form as . Pass the vessel's current rotation to evaluate the wrench at its current orientation. The angular velocity of the vessel, in reference frame . This adds the solid-body rotation term to each part's local airflow and the per-part rigid-body angular drag the game applies, together giving the aerodynamic damping force and torque. Pass a zero vector to evaluate the static wrench relative to the reference frame. The universal time used for the atmospheric ephemeris. It selects the body/Sun geometry used for temperature and density, but does not change or propagate or any of the state arguments. A pair containing the aerodynamic force in newtons followed by the aerodynamic torque in newton-meters about the vessel's center of mass. Both are vectors in reference frame . The position and velocity describe the hypothetical center-of-mass state. The position, velocity, rotation and angular velocity arguments, and both returned vectors, are expressed in reference frame . For future-state prediction, is recommended so that the spatial state has unambiguous inertial semantics. This is an instantaneous rigid-body result based on the vessel's current parts, drag cubes and control-surface state. When Ferram Aerospace Research is installed the angular velocity and arguments are ignored.

Flight_SimulateAerodynamicTorqueAt.documentation: Simulate and return the total aerodynamic torque acting on the vessel about its center of mass, if it were traveling with the given velocity, at the given position, orientation and angular velocity, in the atmosphere of the given celestial body. The celestial body whose atmosphere the torque is simulated in. The position of the vessel, in reference frame . The velocity of the vessel, in reference frame . The orientation of the vessel, in reference frame , in the same form as . Pass the vessel's current rotation to evaluate the torque at its current orientation. The angular velocity of the vessel, in reference frame . This adds the solid-body rotation term to each part's local airflow and the per-part rigid-body angular drag the game applies, together giving the aerodynamic damping torque. Pass a zero vector to evaluate the static torque. A vector pointing along the axis of the torque, with its magnitude equal to the strength of the torque in newton-meters, in reference frame . The position, velocity, rotation and angular velocity arguments, and the returned torque, are all expressed in reference frame . When Ferram Aerospace Research is installed the angular velocity argument is ignored. Atmospheric temperature and density are evaluated at the current universal time. This is the ideal rigid-body aerodynamic torque, summed from the per-part forces about the center of mass. A vessel may not visibly rotate by the full amount when a large aerodynamic force acts on a small part far from the center of mass, because the game applies each part's force to that part and propagates it through the joints rather than to the vessel as a rigid body.

Flight_get_Drag.documentation: The aerodynamic drag currently acting on the vessel. A vector pointing in the direction of the force, with its magnitude equal to the strength of the force in Newtons.

Flight_get_AerodynamicAcceleration.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The acceleration of the vessel due to the total aerodynamic forces acting on it
(<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Flight.AerodynamicForce" /> divided by the vessel's mass),
in reference frame <see cref="T:SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame" />.
</summary>
<returns>A vector pointing in the direction that the vessel is accelerated,
with its magnitude equal to the acceleration in <math>m/s^2</math>.</returns>
</doc>

Flight_get_LiftAcceleration.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The acceleration of the vessel due to <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Flight.Lift" />
(the aerodynamic lift divided by the vessel's mass),
in reference frame <see cref="T:SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame" />.
</summary>
<returns>A vector pointing in the direction that the vessel is accelerated,
with its magnitude equal to the acceleration in <math>m/s^2</math>.</returns>
</doc>

Flight_get_DragAcceleration.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The acceleration of the vessel due to <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Flight.Drag" />
(the aerodynamic drag divided by the vessel's mass),
in reference frame <see cref="T:SpaceCenter.ReferenceFrame" />.
</summary>
<returns>A vector pointing in the direction that the vessel is accelerated,
with its magnitude equal to the acceleration in <math>m/s^2</math>.</returns>
</doc>

Flight_get_SpeedOfSound.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The speed of sound, in the atmosphere around the vessel, in <math>m/s</math>.
</summary>
</doc>

Flight_get_Mach.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The speed of the vessel, in multiples of the speed of sound.
</summary>
</doc>

Flight_get_ReynoldsNumber.documentation: The vessels Reynolds number. Requires Ferram Aerospace Research.

Flight_get_TrueAirSpeed.documentation: The true air speed of the vessel, in meters per second.

Flight_get_EquivalentAirSpeed.documentation: The equivalent air speed of the vessel, in meters per second.

Flight_get_TerminalVelocity.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
An estimate of the current terminal velocity of the vessel, in meters per second.
This is the speed at which the drag forces cancel out the force of gravity.
</summary>
</doc>

Flight_get_AngleOfAttack.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The pitch angle between the orientation of the vessel and its velocity vector,
in degrees.
</summary>
</doc>

Flight_get_SideslipAngle.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The yaw angle between the orientation of the vessel and its velocity vector, in degrees.
</summary>
</doc>

Flight_get_TotalAirTemperature.documentation: The total air temperature of the atmosphere around the vessel, in Kelvin. This includes the and the vessel's kinetic energy.

Flight_get_StaticAirTemperature.documentation: The static (ambient) temperature of the atmosphere around the vessel, in Kelvin.

Flight_get_StallFraction.documentation: The current amount of stall, between 0 and 1. A value greater than 0.005 indicates a minor stall and a value greater than 0.5 indicates a large-scale stall. Requires Ferram Aerospace Research.

Flight_get_DragCoefficient.documentation: The coefficient of drag. This is the amount of drag produced by the vessel. It depends on air speed, air density and wing area. Requires Ferram Aerospace Research.

Flight_get_LiftCoefficient.documentation: The coefficient of lift. This is the amount of lift produced by the vessel, and depends on air speed, air density and wing area. Requires Ferram Aerospace Research.

Flight_get_ThrustSpecificFuelConsumption.documentation: The thrust specific fuel consumption for the jet engines on the vessel. This is a measure of the efficiency of the engines, with a lower value indicating a more efficient vessel. This value is the number of Newtons of fuel that are burned, per hour, to produce one newton of thrust. Requires Ferram Aerospace Research.

LaunchSite_get_EditorFacility.documentation:

</doc>

The reference frame that is fixed relative to the maneuver node's burn.
<list type="bullet"><item><description>The origin is at the position of the maneuver node.</description></item><item><description>The y-axis points in the direction of the burn.</description></item><item><description>The x-axis and z-axis point in arbitrary but fixed directions.</description></item></list></summary>

Node_get_OrbitalReferenceFrame.documentation:

orbit, at the position of the maneuver node.</description></item><item><description>The y-axis points in the orbital prograde direction of the original
orbit, at the position of the maneuver node.</description></item><item><description>The z-axis points in the orbital normal direction of the original orbit,
at the position of the maneuver node.</description></item></list></summary>
</doc>

Returns the times at closest approach and corresponding distances, to a target orbit.

Orbit_TrueAnomalyAtAN.documentation:

Orbit_TrueAnomalyAtDN.documentation:

The true anomaly of the descending node with the given target orbit.

</doc>

Orbit_RelativeInclination.documentation:
<doc>

Relative inclination of this orbit and the target orbit, in radians.
</summary>
<param name="target">Target orbit.</param>
</doc>

Orbit_get_Body.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The celestial body (e.g. planet or moon) around which the object is orbiting.
</summary>
</doc>

Orbit_get_Apoapsis.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Gets the apoapsis of the orbit, in meters, from the center of mass
of the body being orbited.
</summary>
<remarks>
For the apoapsis altitude reported on the in-game map view,
use <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Orbit.ApoapsisAltitude" />.
</remarks>
</doc>

Orbit_get_Periapsis.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The periapsis of the orbit, in meters, from the center of mass
of the body being orbited.
</summary>
<remarks>
For the periapsis altitude reported on the in-game map view,
use <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Orbit.PeriapsisAltitude" />.
</remarks>
</doc>

Orbit_get_ApoapsisAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The apoapsis of the orbit, in meters, above the sea level of the body being orbited.
</summary>
<remarks>
This is equal to <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Orbit.Apoapsis" /> minus the equatorial radius of the body.
</remarks>
</doc>

Orbit_get_PeriapsisAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The periapsis of the orbit, in meters, above the sea level of the body being orbited.
</summary>
<remarks>
This is equal to <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Orbit.Periapsis" /> minus the equatorial radius of the body.
</remarks>
</doc>

Orbit_get_SemiMajorAxis.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The semi-major axis of the orbit, in meters.
</summary>
</doc>

Orbit_get_SemiMinorAxis.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The semi-minor axis of the orbit, in meters.
</summary>
</doc>

Orbit_get_Radius.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current radius of the orbit, in meters. This is the distance between the center
of mass of the object in orbit, and the center of mass of the body around which it
is orbiting.
</summary>
<remarks>
This value will change over time if the orbit is elliptical.
</remarks>
</doc>

Orbit_get_Speed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current orbital speed of the object in meters per second.
</summary>
<remarks>
This value will change over time if the orbit is elliptical.
</remarks>
</doc>

Orbit_get_TimeToApoapsis.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The time until the object reaches apoapsis, in seconds.
</summary>
</doc>

Orbit_get_TimeToPeriapsis.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The time until the object reaches periapsis, in seconds.
</summary>
</doc>

Orbit_get_Inclination.documentation: The inclination of the orbit, in radians.

Orbit_get_LongitudeOfAscendingNode.documentation: The longitude of the ascending node, in radians. For a near-equatorial orbit, the ascending node is ill-defined and this value may vary erratically over time.

Orbit_get_ArgumentOfPeriapsis.documentation: The argument of periapsis, in radians. For a near-circular orbit, the periapsis is ill-defined and this value may vary erratically over time.

Orbit_get_Epoch.documentation: The time since the epoch (the point at which the mean anomaly at epoch was measured, in seconds.

Orbit_get_NextOrbit.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
If the object is going to change sphere of influence in the future, returns the new
orbit after the change. Otherwise returns <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Orbit_get_TimeToSOIChange.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The time until the object changes sphere of influence, in seconds. Returns <c>NaN</c>
if the object is not going to change sphere of influence.
</summary>
</doc>

Orbit_get_OrbitalSpeed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current orbital speed in meters per second.
</summary>
</doc>

Orbit_get_OrbitalEnergy.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The specific orbital energy of the orbit, in Joules per kilogram
(equivalently, meters squared per second squared). This is the sum
of the orbit's specific kinetic and potential energy, and is
negative for a bound (elliptical) orbit.
</summary>
</doc>

ReferenceFrame_static_CreateRelative.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Create a relative reference frame. This is a custom reference frame
whose components offset the components of a parent reference frame.
</summary>
<param name="referenceFrame">The parent reference frame on which to
base this reference frame.</param>
<param name="position">The offset of the position of the origin,
as a position vector. Defaults to <math>(0, 0, 0)</math></param>
<param name="rotation">The rotation to apply to the parent frames rotation,
as a quaternion of the form <math>(x, y, z, w)</math>.
Defaults to <math>(0, 0, 0, 1)</math> (i.e. no rotation)</param>
<param name="velocity">The linear velocity to offset the parent frame by,
as a vector pointing in the direction of travel, whose magnitude is the speed in
meters per second. Defaults to <math>(0, 0, 0)</math>.</param>
<param name="angularVelocity">The angular velocity to offset the parent frame by,
as a vector. This vector points in the direction of the axis of rotation,
and its magnitude is the speed of the rotation in radians per second.
Defaults to <math>(0, 0, 0)</math>.</param>
</doc>

ReferenceFrame_static_CreateHybrid.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Create a hybrid reference frame. This is a custom reference frame
whose components inherited from other reference frames.
</summary>
<param name="position">The reference frame providing the position of the origin.</param>
<param name="rotation">The reference frame providing the rotation of the frame.</param>
<param name="velocity">The reference frame providing the linear velocity of the frame.
</param>
<param name="angularVelocity">The reference frame providing the angular velocity
of the frame.</param>
<remarks>
The <paramref name="position" /> reference frame is required but all other
reference frames are optional. If omitted, they are set to the
<paramref name="position" /> reference frame.
</remarks>
</doc>

ResourceTransfer_static_Start.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Start transferring a resource transfer between a pair of parts. The transfer will move
at most <paramref name="maxAmount" /> units of the resource, depending on how much of

destination part.

Vessel_get_PhysicsRange.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The distance from the active vessel, in meters, out to which this vessel keeps running
its physics simulation — and so stays controllable, able to burn its engines and
respond to its autopilot. Setting this raises the vessel out of the stock physics
bubble, so that it keeps flying while the active vessel is far away. Set to zero to
restore the game's default range.
</summary>
<remarks>
This always reports the vessel's live range, so reading it when no range has been set
gives the game's default for the vessel's current <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.Situation" /> — which is
much shorter than the distance at which the vessel unloads. In orbit a vessel is put
on rails just 350m away, long before it unloads at 2.5km, and a vessel on rails
produces no thrust and ignores control input even though it is still loaded.

There is a 10% margin below the range, so that a vessel hovering at the threshold does
not repeatedly drop out of the simulation and rejoin it. The vessel leaves the
simulation at the distance set here, and rejoins it at 90% of that distance; in
between it keeps whichever state it is already in.

The requested range applies in every situation. The game's own defaults are not
uniform — a vessel flying in atmosphere stays loaded out to 22.5km — so setting a
small range can shorten the range such a vessel would otherwise have had.

A range lasts until it is set back to zero or the game is exited. Unlike most state a
client sets, it is not released when that client disconnects, because dropping a
distant vessel back to the default range would put it on-rails part way through a
maneuver.

Holding a vessel off-rails a long way from the active vessel costs performance, and
accumulates positional error that can destroy it. Raise the range on the vessels that
need it, by as little as they need.
</remarks>
</doc>

Vessel_get_SurfaceReferenceFrame.documentation: The reference frame that is fixed relative to the vessel, and orientated with the surface of the body being orbited. The altitude of the waypoint above sea level, in meters.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_set_MeanAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The altitude of the waypoint above sea level, in meters.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_SurfaceAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The altitude of the waypoint above the surface of the body or sea level,
whichever is closer, in meters.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_set_SurfaceAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The altitude of the waypoint above the surface of the body or sea level,
whichever is closer, in meters.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_BedrockAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The altitude of the waypoint above the surface of the body, in meters.
When over water, this is the altitude above the sea floor.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_set_BedrockAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The altitude of the waypoint above the surface of the body, in meters.
When over water, this is the altitude above the sea floor.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_NearSurface.documentation:
<doc>
<summary><c>true</c> if the waypoint is near to the surface of a body.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_Grounded.documentation:
<doc>
<summary><c>true</c> if the waypoint is attached to the ground.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_Index.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The integer index of this waypoint within its cluster of sibling waypoints.
In other words, when you have a cluster of waypoints called "Somewhere Alpha",
"Somewhere Beta" and "Somewhere Gamma", the alpha site has index 0, the beta
site has index 1 and the gamma site has index 2.
When <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Waypoint.Clustered" /> is <c>false</c>, this is zero.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_Clustered.documentation:
<doc>
<summary><c>true</c> if this waypoint is part of a set of clustered waypoints with greek letter
names appended (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, etc).
If <c>true</c>, there is a one-to-one correspondence with the greek letter name and
the <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Waypoint.Index" />.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_HasContract.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the waypoint belongs to a contract.
</summary>
</doc>

WaypointManager_AddWaypoint.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Creates a waypoint at the given position at ground level, and returns a
<see cref="T:SpaceCenter.Waypoint" /> object that can be used to modify it.
</summary>
<param name="latitude">Latitude of the waypoint.</param>
<param name="longitude">Longitude of the waypoint.</param>
<param name="body">Celestial body the waypoint is attached to.</param>
<param name="name">Name of the waypoint.</param>
<returns></returns>
</doc>

WaypointManager_AddWaypointAtAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Creates a waypoint at the given position and altitude, and returns a
<see cref="T:SpaceCenter.Waypoint" /> object that can be used to modify it.
</summary>
<param name="latitude">Latitude of the waypoint.</param>
<param name="longitude">Longitude of the waypoint.</param>
<param name="altitude">Altitude (above sea level) of the waypoint.</param>
<param name="body">Celestial body the waypoint is attached to.</param>
<param name="name">Name of the waypoint.</param>
<returns></returns>
</doc>

WaypointManager_get_Waypoints.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A list of all existing waypoints.
</summary>
</doc>

WaypointManager_get_Colors.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
An example map of known color - seed pairs.
Any other integers may be used as seed.
</summary>
</doc>

ActionGroupAction_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part that the action acts on.
</summary>
</doc>

ActionGroupAction_get_Module.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part module that the action belongs to. Returns <c>null</c> for a
part-level action that is not associated with a module. This only occurs when
the Extended Action Groups mod is installed, as it can assign actions defined
directly on a part, rather than on one of its modules, to an action group.
</summary>
</doc>

ActionGroupAction_get_Name.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The human-readable name of the action, as shown in the action group editor.
</summary>
</doc>

ActionGroupAction_get_Id.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The non-localized identifier for the action.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this antenna.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_State.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current state of the antenna.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_Deployed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the antenna is deployed.
</summary>
<remarks>
Fixed antennas are always deployed.
Returns an error if you try to deploy a fixed antenna.
</remarks>
</doc>

Antenna_set_Deployed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the antenna is deployed.
</summary>
<remarks>
Fixed antennas are always deployed.
Returns an error if you try to deploy a fixed antenna.
</remarks>
</doc>

Antenna_get_CanTransmit.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether data can be transmitted by this antenna.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_AllowPartial.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether partial data transmission is permitted.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_set_AllowPartial.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether partial data transmission is permitted.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_Combinable.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the antenna can be combined with other antennae on the vessel
to boost the power.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_CombinableExponent.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Exponent used to calculate the combined power of multiple antennae on a vessel.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_PacketInterval.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Interval between sending packets in seconds.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_PacketSize.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Amount of data sent per packet in Mits.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_PacketResourceCost.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Units of electric charge consumed per packet sent.
</summary>
</doc>

CargoBay_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this cargo bay.
</summary>
</doc>

CargoBay_get_State.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The state of the cargo bay.
</summary>
<remarks>
This describes where the bay's doors are, which is not the same as whether the parts
inside are sheltered: a bay whose open end has nothing attached to it never shelters
anything, however tightly shut it is. Use <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Shielded" /> for that.

A cargo bay is never <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.DeployableState.Broken" />, as the game
does not track damage for them.
</remarks>
</doc>

CargoBay_get_Open.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the cargo bay is open.
</summary>
</doc>

CargoBay_set_Open.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the cargo bay is open.
</summary>
</doc>

ConfigNode_HasValue.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Returns <c>true</c> if the node has a value with the given name.
</summary>
<param name="name">Name of the value.</param>
</doc>

ConfigNode_GetValue.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Returns the value with the given name. If there is more than one value with
the given name, the first is returned. Throws an exception if there is no
value with the given name.
</summary>
<param name="name">Name of the value.</param>
</doc>

ConfigNode_GetValues.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Returns all of the values with the given name, as a list.
</summary>
<param name="name">Name of the values.</param>
</doc>

ConfigNode_HasNode.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Returns <c>true</c> if the node has a child node with the given name.
</summary>
<param name="name">Name of the child node.</param>
</doc>

ConfigNode_GetNode.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Returns the child node with the given name. If there is more than one child
node with the given name, the first is returned. Throws an exception if there
is no child node with the given name.
</summary>
<param name="name">Name of the child node.</param>
</doc>

ConfigNode_GetNodes.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Returns all of the child nodes with the given name, as a list.
</summary>
<param name="name">Name of the child nodes.</param>
</doc>

ConfigNode_get_Name.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The name of the configuration node. For example "MODULE".
</summary>
</doc>

ConfigNode_get_Values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The values stored in the node, as a dictionary mapping names to values.
</summary>
<remarks>
If a name appears more than once, only the first value is included. Use
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ConfigNode.GetValues" /> to get all of the values with a given name.
</remarks>
</doc>

ConfigNode_get_Nodes.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The child nodes contained in this node.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this control surface.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_PitchEnabled.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has pitch control enabled.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_PitchEnabled.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has pitch control enabled.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_YawEnabled.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has yaw control enabled.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_YawEnabled.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has yaw control enabled.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_RollEnabled.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has roll control enabled.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_RollEnabled.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has roll control enabled.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_AuthorityLimiter.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The authority limiter for the control surface, which controls how far the
control surface will move.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_AuthorityLimiter.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The authority limiter for the control surface, which controls how far the
control surface will move.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_Inverted.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface movement is inverted.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_Inverted.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface movement is inverted.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_Deployed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has been fully deployed.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_Deployed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has been fully deployed.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_DeflectionOverride.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface deflection is being set directly, bypassing the vessel's
normal flight control. When enabled, the surface holds the deflection set by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.Deflection" /> instead of responding to pitch, yaw and roll control inputs.
The prior state is restored when the override is released, when the
controlling client disconnects, or when the vessel changes.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_DeflectionOverride.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface deflection is being set directly, bypassing the vessel's
normal flight control. When enabled, the surface holds the deflection set by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.Deflection" /> instead of responding to pitch, yaw and roll control inputs.
The prior state is restored when the override is released, when the
controlling client disconnects, or when the vessel changes.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_Deflection.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The deflection command applied when <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.DeflectionOverride" /> is enabled, as a
value between -1 and 1, mapped onto the surface's deploy angle range.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_Deflection.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The deflection command applied when <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.DeflectionOverride" /> is enabled, as a
value between -1 and 1, mapped onto the surface's deploy angle range.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_SurfaceArea.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Surface area of the control surface in <math>m^2</math>.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_AvailableTorque.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The available torque, in Newton meters, that can be produced by this control surface,
in the positive and negative pitch, roll and yaw axes of the vessel. These axes
correspond to the coordinate axes of the <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.ReferenceFrame" />.
</summary>
</doc>

Decoupler_Decouple.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Fires the decoupler. Returns the new vessel created when the decoupler fires.
Throws an exception if the decoupler has already fired.
</summary>
<remarks>
When called, the active vessel may change. It is therefore possible that,
after calling this function, the object(s) returned by previous call(s) to
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ActiveVessel" /> no longer refer to the active vessel.
</remarks>
</doc>

Decoupler_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this decoupler.
</summary>
</doc>

Decoupler_get_Staged.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the decoupler is enabled in the staging sequence.
</summary>
</doc>

Decoupler_get_Impulse.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The impulse that the decoupler imparts when it is fired, in Newton seconds.
</summary>
</doc>

Decoupler_get_IsOmniDecoupler.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the decoupler is an omni-decoupler (e.g. stack separator)
</summary>
</doc>

Decoupler_get_AttachedPart.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part attached to this decoupler's explosive node.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_Undock.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Undocks the docking port and returns the new <see cref="T:SpaceCenter.Vessel" /> that is created.
This method can be called for either docking port in a docked pair.
Throws an exception if the docking port is not docked to anything.
</summary>
<remarks>
When called, the active vessel may change. It is therefore possible that,
after calling this function, the object(s) returned by previous call(s) to
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ActiveVessel" /> no longer refer to the active vessel.
</remarks>
</doc>

DockingPort_Position.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The position of the docking port, in the given reference frame.
</summary>
<returns>The position as a vector.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
position vector is in.</param>
</doc>

DockingPort_Direction.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The direction that docking port points in, in the given reference frame.
</summary>
<returns>The direction as a unit vector.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
direction is in.</param>
</doc>

DockingPort_Rotation.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rotation of the docking port, in the given reference frame.
</summary>
<returns>The rotation as a quaternion of the form <math>(x, y, z, w)</math>.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
rotation is in.</param>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this docking port.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_State.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current state of the docking port.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_DockedPart.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part that this docking port is docked to. Returns <c>null</c> if this
docking port is not docked to anything.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_ReengageDistance.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The distance a docking port must move away when it undocks before it
becomes ready to dock with another port, in meters.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_HasShield.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the docking port has a shield.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_Shielded.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The state of the docking ports shield, if it has one.

Returns <c>true</c> if the docking port has a shield, and the shield is
closed. Otherwise returns <c>false</c>. When set to <c>true</c>, the shield is
closed, and when set to <c>false</c> the shield is opened. If the docking
port does not have a shield, setting this attribute has no effect.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_set_Shielded.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The state of the docking ports shield, if it has one.

Returns <c>true</c> if the docking port has a shield, and the shield is
closed. Otherwise returns <c>false</c>. When set to <c>true</c>, the shield is
closed, and when set to <c>false</c> the shield is opened. If the docking
port does not have a shield, setting this attribute has no effect.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_CanRotate.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the docking port can be commanded to rotate while docked.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_RotationLocked.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Lock rotation. When locked, allows auto-strut to work across the joint.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_set_RotationLocked.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Lock rotation. When locked, allows auto-strut to work across the joint.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_ReferenceFrame.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The reference frame that is fixed relative to this docking port, and
oriented with the port.
<list type="bullet"><item><description>The origin is at the position of the docking port.
</description></item><item><description>The axes rotate with the docking port.</description></item><item><description>The x-axis points out to the right side of the docking port.
</description></item><item><description>The y-axis points in the direction the docking port is facing.
</description></item><item><description>The z-axis points out of the bottom off the docking port.
</description></item></list></summary>
<remarks>
This reference frame is not necessarily equivalent to the reference frame
for the part, returned by <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.ReferenceFrame" />.
</remarks>
</doc>

Engine_AvailableThrustAt.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The amount of thrust, in Newtons, that would be produced by the engine
when activated and with its throttle set to 100%.
Returns zero if the engine does not have any fuel.
Takes the given pressure into account.
</summary>
<param name="pressure">Atmospheric pressure in atmospheres</param>
</doc>

Engine_MaxThrustAt.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The amount of thrust, in Newtons, that would be produced by the engine
when activated and fueled, with its throttle and throttle limiter set to 100%.
Takes the given pressure into account.
</summary>
<param name="pressure">Atmospheric pressure in atmospheres</param>
</doc>

Engine_SpecificImpulseAt.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The specific impulse of the engine under the given pressure, in seconds. Returns zero
if the engine is not active.
</summary>
<param name="pressure">Atmospheric pressure in atmospheres</param>
</doc>

Engine_ToggleThrustReversal.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Toggle the engine's thrust reverser. Raises an exception if the engine
does not have a thrust reverser (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.CanReverseThrust" />).
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this engine.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Active.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine is active. Setting this attribute may have no effect,
depending on <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.CanShutdown" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.CanRestart" />.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_Active.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine is active. Setting this attribute may have no effect,
depending on <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.CanShutdown" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.CanRestart" />.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Thrust.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current amount of thrust being produced by the engine, in Newtons.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_AvailableThrust.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The amount of thrust, in Newtons, that would be produced by the engine
when activated and with its throttle set to 100%.
Returns zero if the engine does not have any fuel.
Takes the engine's current <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.ThrustLimit" /> and atmospheric conditions
into account.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_MaxThrust.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The amount of thrust, in Newtons, that would be produced by the engine
when activated and fueled, with its throttle and throttle limiter set to 100%.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_MaxVacuumThrust.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The maximum amount of thrust that can be produced by the engine in a
vacuum, in Newtons. This is the amount of thrust produced by the engine
when activated, <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.ThrustLimit" /> is set to 100%, the main
vessel's throttle is set to 100% and the engine is in a vacuum.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_ThrustLimit.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The thrust limiter of the engine. A value between 0 and 1. Setting this
attribute may have no effect, for example the thrust limit for a solid
rocket booster cannot be changed in flight.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_ThrustLimit.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The thrust limiter of the engine. A value between 0 and 1. Setting this
attribute may have no effect, for example the thrust limit for a solid
rocket booster cannot be changed in flight.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Thrusters.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The components of the engine that generate thrust.
</summary>
<remarks>
For example, this corresponds to the rocket nozzel on a solid rocket booster,
or the individual nozzels on a RAPIER engine.
The overall thrust produced by the engine, as reported by <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.AvailableThrust" />,
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.MaxThrust" /> and others, is the sum of the thrust generated by each thruster.
</remarks>
</doc>

Engine_get_SpecificImpulse.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current specific impulse of the engine, in seconds. Returns zero
if the engine is not active.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_VacuumSpecificImpulse.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The vacuum specific impulse of the engine, in seconds.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_KerbinSeaLevelSpecificImpulse.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The specific impulse of the engine at sea level on Kerbin, in seconds.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_PropellantNames.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The names of the propellants that the engine consumes.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Propellants.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The propellants that the engine consumes.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_PropellantRatios.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The ratio of resources that the engine consumes. A dictionary mapping resource names
to the ratio at which they are consumed by the engine.
</summary>
<remarks>
For example, if the ratios are 0.6 for LiquidFuel and 0.4 for Oxidizer, then for every
0.6 units of LiquidFuel that the engine burns, it will burn 0.4 units of Oxidizer.
</remarks>
</doc>

Engine_get_HasFuel.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine has any fuel available.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Flameout.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine has flamed out - it is active but has run out of
propellant, so it is producing no thrust. This is the signal a client
can use to decide when to activate the next stage. Note that on a
vessel with drop tanks or asparagus staging some engines can flame out
while others keep burning.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Throttle.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current throttle setting for the engine. A value between 0 and 1.
This is not necessarily the same as the vessel's main throttle
setting, as some engines take time to adjust their throttle
(such as jet engines), or independent throttle may be enabled.

When the engine's independent throttle is enabled
(see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.IndependentThrottle" />), can be used to set the throttle percentage.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_Throttle.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current throttle setting for the engine. A value between 0 and 1.
This is not necessarily the same as the vessel's main throttle
setting, as some engines take time to adjust their throttle
(such as jet engines), or independent throttle may be enabled.

When the engine's independent throttle is enabled
(see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.IndependentThrottle" />), can be used to set the throttle percentage.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_ThrottleLocked.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Control.Throttle" /> affects the engine. For example,
this is <c>true</c> for liquid fueled rockets, and <c>false</c> for solid rocket
boosters.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_IndependentThrottle.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the independent throttle is enabled for the engine.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_IndependentThrottle.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the independent throttle is enabled for the engine.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_CanRestart.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine can be restarted once shutdown. If the engine cannot be shutdown,
returns <c>false</c>. For example, this is <c>true</c> for liquid fueled rockets
and <c>false</c> for solid rocket boosters.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_CanShutdown.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine can be shutdown once activated. For example, this is
<c>true</c> for liquid fueled rockets and <c>false</c> for solid rocket boosters.

Part_get_ThermalInternalFlux.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rate at which heat energy is begin generated by the part.
For example, some engines generate heat by combusting fuel.
Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts.
A positive value means the part is gaining heat energy, and negative means it is losing
heat energy.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ThermalConductionFlux.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rate at which heat energy is conducting into or out of the part via contact with
other parts. Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts.
A positive value means the part is gaining heat energy, and negative means it is
losing heat energy.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ThermalConvectionFlux.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rate at which heat energy is convecting into or out of the part from the
surrounding atmosphere. Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts.
A positive value means the part is gaining heat energy, and negative means it is
losing heat energy.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ThermalRadiationFlux.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rate at which heat energy is radiating into or out of the part from the surrounding
environment. Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts.
A positive value means the part is gaining heat energy, and negative means it is
losing heat energy.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ThermalSkinToInternalFlux.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rate at which heat energy is transferring between the part's skin and its internals.
Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts.
A positive value means the part's internals are gaining heat energy,
and negative means its skin is gaining heat energy.
</summary>
</doc>

position vector is in.</param>
</doc>

<doc>
<summary>
The direction of the force generated by the thruster, in the given reference frame.
This is opposite to the direction in which the thruster expels propellant.
For gimballed engines, this takes into account the current rotation of the gimbal.

<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned

initial position (no gimballing), in the given reference frame.

position vector is in.</param>
<remarks>
This position can move when the gimbal rotates. This is because the thrust position and
gimbal position are not necessarily the same.
</remarks>
</doc>

Thruster_InitialThrustDirection.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The direction of the force generated by the thruster, when the engine is in its
initial position (no gimballing), in the given reference frame.
This is opposite to the direction in which the thruster expels propellant.
</summary>
<returns>The direction as a unit vector.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
direction is in.</param>

<list type="bullet"><item><description>

(<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Thruster.ThrustPosition" />).</description></item><item><description>
The axes rotate with the thrust direction.
This is the direction in which the thruster expels propellant, including any gimballing.
</description></item><item><description>The y-axis points along the thrust direction.</description></item><item><description>The x-axis and z-axis are perpendicular to the thrust direction.

ClosestApproach.documentation:

<summary>
A close approach between an orbit and a target orbit. Obtained by calling
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Orbit.NextClosestApproach" /> or <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Orbit.ClosestApproaches" />.
</summary>

CommLink.documentation:

Contracts manager.

Control.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Used to manipulate the controls of a vessel. This includes adjusting the
throttle, enabling/disabling systems such as SAS and RCS, or altering the
direction in which the vessel is pointing.
Obtained by calling <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.Control" />.
</summary>
<remarks>
Control inputs (pitch, yaw, roll, translation, wheel throttle, wheel steering
and the custom axes) are zeroed when all clients that have set one or more of
these inputs are no longer connected. The throttle is an exception: it keeps
its value when clients disconnect.
</remarks>
</doc>

CrewMember.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Represents crew in a vessel. Can be obtained using <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.Crew" />.
</summary>
</doc>

Flight.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Used to get flight telemetry for a vessel, by calling <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.Flight" />.
All of the information returned by this class is given in the reference frame
passed to that method.
Obtained by calling <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.Flight" />.
</summary>
<remarks>
To get orbital information, such as the apoapsis or inclination, see <see cref="T:SpaceCenter.Orbit" />.
</remarks>
</doc>

LaunchSite.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A place where craft can be launched from.
More of these can be added with mods like Kerbal Konstructs.
</summary>
</doc>

Node.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Represents a maneuver node. Can be created using <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Control.AddNode" />.
</summary>
</doc>

Orbit.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Describes an orbit. For example, the orbit of a vessel, obtained by calling
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.Orbit" />, or a celestial body, obtained by calling
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.CelestialBody.Orbit" />.
</summary>
</doc>

ReferenceFrame.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Represents a reference frame for positions, rotations and
velocities. Contains:
<list type="bullet"><item><description>The position of the origin.</description></item><item><description>The directions of the x, y and z axes.</description></item><item><description>The linear velocity of the frame.</description></item><item><description>The angular velocity of the frame.</description></item></list></summary>
<remarks>
This class does not contain any properties or methods. It is only
used as a parameter to other functions.
</remarks>
</doc>

Resource.documentation:

</summary>
</doc>

Resources.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Represents the collection of resources stored in a vessel, stage or part.
Created by calling <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.Resources" />,
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.ResourcesInDecoupleStage" /> or
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Resources" />.
</summary>
</doc>

Stage.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A single stage of a vessel. Obtain activation (burn) stages from
<c>Vessel.Stages</c> / <c>Vessel.StageAt</c>, and decouple stages from
<c>Vessel.DecoupleStages</c> / <c>Vessel.DecoupleStageAt</c>.
</summary>
<remarks>
Delta-v, thrust, TWR, specific impulse, burn time and mass members are only
available on activation stages. On decouple stages those members throw
InvalidOperationException because stock delta-v data does not
apply. Thrust is reported in newtons and masses in kilograms (stock values
are converted from kilonewtons and tonnes).
</remarks>
</doc>

Vessel.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
These objects are used to interact with vessels in KSP. This includes getting
orbital and flight data, manipulating control inputs and managing resources.
Created using <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ActiveVessel" /> or <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessels" />.
</summary>
</doc>

MitigationMode.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Controls one of the auto-pilot's individually-toggleable oscillation mitigations
(<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.OscillationBandwidthFloorMode" />,
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.OscillationFeedforwardMode" />,
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.OscillationOutputFilterMode" />).
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Automatic
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The default: the mitigation engages automatically, driven by the runtime oscillation
detector and the hold gate. Rigid vessels are left untouched.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Off
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The mitigation never engages. The other mitigations are unaffected.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Forced
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The mitigation is fully engaged at all times, regardless of what the oscillation
detector reports.
</summary>
</doc>

RateFilterMode.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Controls the auto-pilot's rate-feedback filtering for an axis group — the mitigation that
removes a structural oscillation (wobble) from the measured angular velocity before the
control loops consume it.
See <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.PitchYawRateFilterMode" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.RollRateFilterMode" />.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Automatic
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The default. The auto-pilot detects structural oscillation at runtime, estimates its
frequency and routes it to the appropriate filter: a notch for a low-frequency mode
near the control band, a low-pass for a high-frequency mode, or a broadband low-pass
while the frequency is not yet known. Rigid vessels are left untouched.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Off
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
No rate filtering. The other oscillation mitigations are unaffected.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Notch
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Force a notch filter at the manually set frequency
(<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.PitchYawOscillationFrequency" /> /
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.RollOscillationFrequency" />), for a vessel whose structural mode
is known in advance.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: LowPass
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Force a low-pass filter derived from the manually set frequency.
</summary>
</doc>
